report.summary: Police arrested five men in Água Clara after a tip about suspected drug dealing led to searches and follow-up investigations. The operation found 59 cannabis bricks weighing about 54 kg, plus about 500 g with another suspect, and also involved cocaine seizures.

open_questions: The 54 kg of bricks and about 500 g found with another suspect are the separately quantified cannabis amounts; the cannabis portions found at the first suspect's home were not weighed separately.
RCN67 gives a combined total of about 54.64 kg of marijuana and cocaine, which cannot be used as a cannabis-only total.
The sources describe the cannabis as marijuana or material resembling marijuana; no laboratory confirmation is reported.
No later court outcome for the five men was reported.
report.body:
The operation began on the night of Wednesday 4 November after an anonymous tip
that a vehicle was being used to sell drugs in Água Clara. The tip
concerned a white VW Gol allegedly used to sell drugs in Jardim das Palmeiras. When Military Police located the car, its driver tried to flee but was
stopped after a chase over several blocks. Officers found suspected cocaine
in the car and cannabis portions, a precision scale, packaging materials and
cash at the driver's home. The joint follow-up found two other suspects at
a snack bar and 59 bricks of material resembling marijuana that weighed about 54
kg.

Investigators later found a third suspect with approximately 500 grams of
marijuana and a precision scale. Police also recovered a bag of 19 portions
of cocaine, about 120 grams in total, which investigators said the first suspect
had discarded during the original approach. A 28-year-old man under
investigation for trafficking and wanted on an outstanding arrest warrant was
also located and arrested. RCN67 reported five men arrested in total: four
were booked in flagrante for trafficking and association for trafficking, while
the fifth was arrested under a judicial order. Officers seized a car, a
motorcycle, three scales, three mobile phones, packaging material and about
R$250, in addition to the drugs.

report.body:
Military Police officers arrested a man in Mojuí dos Campos on 12 November 2026
after stopping him at about 17:45 at the intersection of Travessa São Sebastião
and Rua Joana D’Arc. The 35th Military Police Battalion said his wife told
officers that more drugs were at their home on Rua Almirante Barroso in the
Cidade Alta 2 neighbourhood. G1 reported that officers found initial drug
portions on the man; after his wife said he trafficked locally, he confessed and
said more cocaine and marijuana were at home.

At the home, police reported finding 31 packages of a substance resembling
cocaine and 12 packages of a substance resembling marijuana. O Impacto's
itemised inventory also lists one greenish portion resembling marijuana. O
Impacto reported that the home search also yielded R$301 in cash. G1
reported 12 marijuana portions, 31 cocaine packages and R$300 in cash, and said
the seized material was ready for sale.

O Impacto reported that the suspect and seized material were taken to the 16th
Civil Police Section in Santarém and that he remained at the judiciary's
disposal.

report.body:
A joint operation by the Government Railway Police (GRP) and Railway Protection
Force (RPF) was launched at Agartala Railway Station on 13 November 2026 after
police received specific information. At about 9 a.m., Sub-Inspector
Biswajit Das and other Agartala GRPS staff apprehended one man on a bench on
platform 1, in front of the parking area between the RPF post and the
pay-and-use toilet. Police identified him as 19-year-old Niraj Kumar of
Jehanabad district in Bihar.

Officers recovered 5.525 kg of suspected ganja from a pithu bag in his
possession. Railway Police arrested him and registered Agartala GRPS Case
No. 2026GRP080 under sections 20(b)(ii)(B)/29 of the Narcotic Drugs and
Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985. Police estimated the seized substance's
black-market value at approximately ₹2.5 lakh.

Inspector Raju Bhowmik, officer in charge of Agartala Railway Police Station,
gave details of the operation to the media and said railway police would
continue such operations against illegal contraband.

report.body:
Police in Ajdabiya arrested two suspects and referred both to the public
prosecutor after raiding a residential apartment in the city. Ajdabiya
Security's photo caption dates the raid to 22 October 2026. The searched
apartment was on the third floor of a residential building in the city.

The Criminal Investigation Department of the Ajdabiya Security Directorate acted
on information from private sources that narcotics and hallucinogenic pills were
in the apartment. The tip said the items were to be moved to an unknown
place to hide them and cover up distribution activity. Investigators opened
an inquiry, checked the information, notified the department and
investigation-unit chiefs, informed the public prosecutor and obtained legal
authorization before searching the apartment. The search yielded 2
kilograms of hashish, 59 boxes of tramadol containing 5,529 tablets and LYD
16,500 in cash. Another account gave the tramadol total as 39 boxes
containing 3,690 tablets.

The seized goods were hidden in a bag designed to carry children, and the
suspects were taken to the department's headquarters to complete
evidence-gathering procedures. The police unit said the suspects admitted
what was attributed to them during evidence-gathering before referral to the
Public Prosecution for legal action.
